input.rationale: Spend the last unit on the remaining executable question of the configuration line: whether the adopted-and-then-committed configuration remains a configuration the node acts on after a restart. NewRaft derives configuration state only by scanning entries through processConfigurationLogEntry and does not restore the commit index, so restarting the node over the same stores is the decisive observation. Submitted a check product that spends the last audit unit on the remaining executable question of the configuration line: whether the adopted-and-committed configuration survives a restart.

Context from the index: all three findings are confirmed_in_scope, map v7 is the accepted basis, pending_work is empty, and capacity still holds 1 audit unit, 3 semantic reviews and 5 experiments.

Product contents (draft-relative submission.json with plan_restart_consistency.json, harness_restart_consistency.go and one newly acquired source range):

New obligation oblig-restart-config-log-backed (consensus_safety): a restarted server must report as its latest configuration only a configuration encoded by the configuration entry at the index it reports. It is bound to Raft.processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1585-1600, acquired as SR-CONFIG-ENTRY), the only path that derives configuration state from a log entry and the one NewRaft runs over every entry above the snapshot index, with the commit index never persisted or restored.

The check repeats the failed configuration write on a two-node in-memory cluster, lets the node commit the adopted configuration with the fresh peer's vote, then shuts node A down and creates a new Raft instance over the same log, stable store, snapshot store and transport with a fresh FSM. The prerequisite records the failed attempt and the pre-restart committed configuration; the result reports the restarted node's latest and committed voter counts and indexes plus the type of the log entry at the index it reports for its latest configuration. The property is an implication: if the restarted node reports the adopted two-voter configuration, the entry at that index must be a configuration entry — so a persisted phantom configuration would be flagged, while a node that re-derives only the log-backed configuration yields a bounded negative answer that the map's last open question on the configuration behavior was looking for.

Preflight `validate` returned valid=true with no diagnostics. Acceptance, clean-copy execution and the observed result remain with the controller.

question.question: Is a heartbeat delivered through the transport fast path serialized with the main loop before it updates the receiver's term, state and believed leader, or can Raft.appendEntries run concurrently with runFollower/runCandidate on the same instance?

formation.explanation: The leader appends each accepted command as a local log entry for its term (b-dispatch-logs), then each per-peer replication goroutine pushes AppendEntries and reports the highest index the peer has stored (b-leader-replicate). commitment.match/recalculate turn those per-voter match indexes into a quorum index, refusing to commit anything below the first index appended in the leader's term (b-commit-quorum). When the quorum index advances, the leader loop publishes the new commit index and applies the committed prefix (b-leader-commit-apply). The support is 'qualified' because a match index only counts after the follower's log has been shown to agree with the leader's up to the previous entry.

context.explanation: Authority is scoped to a term and to the voter set of the latest configuration. A follower that stops hearing a leader becomes a candidate (b-heartbeat-timeout); the candidate proposes and persists the next term and asks for votes, optionally after a pre-vote round (b-candidate-election, b-prevote), and becomes leader only on a quorum of current voters. Voters decide with term, membership, an already-persisted vote for the term, and log up-to-date-ness (b-vote-grant). A leader abandons the role when it observes a higher term or cannot contact a quorum of current voters (b-leader-stepdown), and it can hand the role over deliberately with a replicated-then-TimeoutNow transfer (b-leadership-transfer).

connection.explanation: A1 and A2 meet on three sourced points. First, the term-start-index rule in the commitment makes the leader's own new-term entry a precondition for committing anything, so a server that merely won an election cannot commit an earlier leader's entries (b-commit-quorum / f-commit-quorum / f-term-vote). Second, the voter set that defines both a winning quorum and the commitment quorum comes from the latest configuration, so membership changes reshape eligibility and commitment together (b-config-change, b-candidate-election / f-config-membership). Third, a follower only counts as support after its log prefix has been shown to match the leader's, and that same AppendEntries handling carries the term/state transitions; losing the term (b-leader-stepdown) discards the commitment that the old term's support created, while a transfer pushes the target to the leader's last index before handing over. Old work is handled by failing every inflight future with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down, so pending client requests cannot be mistaken for applied decisions.

formation.explanation: The leader appends each accepted command as a local log entry for its term (b-dispatch-logs), then each per-peer replication goroutine pushes AppendEntries and reports the highest index the peer has stored (b-leader-replicate). commitment.match/recalculate turn those per-voter match indexes into a quorum index, refusing to commit anything below the first index appended in the leader's term (b-commit-quorum). When the quorum index advances, the leader loop publishes the new commit index and applies the committed prefix (b-leader-commit-apply). The support is 'qualified' because a match index only counts after the follower's log has been shown to agree with the leader's up to the previous entry.

context.explanation: Authority is scoped to a term and to the voter set of the latest configuration. A follower that stops hearing a leader becomes a candidate (b-heartbeat-timeout); the candidate proposes and persists the next term and asks for votes, optionally after a pre-vote round (b-candidate-election, b-prevote), and becomes leader only on a quorum of current voters. Voters decide with term, membership, an already-persisted vote for the term, and log up-to-date-ness (b-vote-grant). A leader abandons the role when it observes a higher term or cannot contact a quorum of current voters (b-leader-stepdown), and it can hand the role over deliberately with a replicated-then-TimeoutNow transfer (b-leadership-transfer).

connection.explanation: A1 and A2 meet on three sourced points. First, the term-start-index rule in the commitment makes the leader's own new-term entry a precondition for committing anything, so a server that merely won an election cannot commit an earlier leader's entries (b-commit-quorum / f-commit-quorum / f-term-vote). Second, the voter set that defines both a winning quorum and the commitment quorum comes from the latest configuration, so membership changes reshape eligibility and commitment together (b-config-change, b-candidate-election / f-config-membership). Third, a follower only counts as support after its log prefix has been shown to match the leader's, and that same AppendEntries handling carries the term/state transitions; losing the term (b-leader-stepdown) discards the commitment that the old term's support created, while a transfer pushes the target to the leader's last index before handing over. Old work is handled by failing every inflight future with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down, so pending client requests cannot be mistaken for applied decisions.
